title: Powers & roots
examples: What is the difference between a power and a root?
How do I find the square root of a large number?
Can you explain why a negative power makes the number small?

explain.say: Today we learn about powers and roots. A power just means repeated multiplication. For example, three squared is three times three. So, 3 squared is 9.
A cube is just a power of three. Five cubed means five multiplied by itself three times. So, 5 cubed is 125.
We write these using index notation. The base stays the same, and the top number is the power. Two to the fourth power is two multiplied by itself four times. It equals 16.
Zero power is special. Any number except zero raised to the power of zero is one. For example, seven to the power of zero is one. This is always true.

Negative powers mean we use fractions. A number to a negative power is one over that number multiplied by itself that many times. So, two to the power of negative two is one divided by four. It equals one over four.

faq.q: What is the difference between squaring and cubing a number?
faq.a: Squaring means multiplying a number by itself two times. Cubing means multiplying that same number by itself three times. You can also ask this by saying 'What is a number to the power of two?' or 'What is a number to the third power?'
asks: How do I find a number cubed?

faq.q: How do I find the square root of a number like 49?
faq.a: The square root asks what number times itself equals the given number. The square root of 49 is 7 because 7 multiplied by 7 is 49. You might also ask 'What number times itself is 49?'
asks: What number multiplied by itself is 49?

faq.q: What does a negative power really mean?
faq.a: A negative power tells you to take the reciprocal, or one over the base raised to the positive power. For example, three to the power of negative one is one over three. You could also ask 'What is the inverse power?'
asks: How do I handle a negative exponent?

faq.q: How do I estimate a root like the square root of 50?
faq.a: You find the perfect squares around the number. Since 7 squared is 49 and 8 squared is 64, the square root of 50 must be just a little bit more than 7. You might also ask 'Which perfect squares surround 50?'

faq.q: Is 1 to any power always one?
faq.a: Yes, any number raised to the power of zero is one. This rule applies even if the base is one. You might also ask 'What is 1 to the power of 10?'
asks: What is 1 raised to any power?
Is 1 raised to zero equal to one?

facts: A number squared means multiplying it by itself two times.
A number cubed means multiplying it by itself three times.
Any non-zero number raised to the power of zero equals one.
The square root of a number finds the value that multiplies by itself to give that number.

quiz.why: Cubing means multiplying the number by itself three times, so 4 times 4 times 4 equals 64.

wrong.0: This is the result of 4 squared, not cubed.
wrong.1: This is just the base number itself.
wrong.2: This is the result of 4 plus 4 plus 4.

quiz.say: What is two to the power of negative three?
quiz.why: A negative power means taking the reciprocal, so it is one over two cubed, which is one over eight.

wrong.0: You cannot simply make the answer negative.
wrong.1: This is the answer for two cubed, forgetting the negative sign.
wrong.2: This incorrectly uses the exponent as the denominator.

quiz.why: Because 5 squared is 25 and 6 squared is 36, the square root of 30 must be between 5 and 6.

wrong.1: This range is too small because 4 squared is 16.
wrong.2: This range is too large because 7 squared is 49.
wrong.3: This confuses the root with the number itself.
